versions.text: Standard: The store and armament equipment are durable such that they resist cracking, corrosion, thermal degradation, delamination, and wear to maintain structural integrity and mechanical operation on all critical structure(s) throughout the specified service life and envelope of the store IAW MIL-M-8856, Durability section and MIL-STD-8591, Service Life section. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis. (1) Initial durability analysis is conducted to verify store structural integrity and mechanical operation for all critical structures commensurate with the specified service life IAW MIL-M- 8856, Analyses, Data, and Reports appendix and MIL-STD-8591, Carriage Design Limit Load appendix. (2) As an alternative to Analysis MoC (1), if the store has been previously cleared for use in similar flight environments, the existing data can be leveraged for a by-similarity comparison to support first flight. Test. (1) Lab test: Test to expected repeated flight loads (determined via analysis or loads survey IAW 17.1.2.1) has been accomplished up to or exceeding 2X the intended number of captive carriage hours necessary for flight test. Sub-assembly or component-level testing of critical structures is permitted in lieu of AUR testing to support initial flight test when there is sufficient design margin. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Examination. (1) Verify the updated durability analysis and FSDT demonstrate durability within the intended service life IAW MIL-M-8856, Structural Demonstration Tests appendix and MIL-STD-8591, Carriage Design Limit Load appendix. (2) Verify that tracking mechanisms are in place to prevent stores exceeding the service life and identify when stores require inspection or repair to maintain durability within the service life. (3) If there is no tracking mechanism (design feature or procedure) to determine the cumulative flight history of the store, then verify that inspection intervals are capable of identifying signs of cracking or structural degradation. Verify that inspection criteria specify non-serviceability limits or end of life. Analysis. (3) Verify the durability analysis is updated with the repeated loads and dynamic environments measured during flight test, correlated to the FSDT, and demonstrates structural integrity and mechanical operation of critical structures commensurate with the specified service life. Test. (2) Ground test: Conduct full-scale durability ground test IAW MIL-M-8856, Laboratory and Ground Tests appendix and MIL-STD-8591, Carriage Design Limit Load appendix using representative loading spectra to 2X the requested service life. Full-scale durability test shows no crack nucleation, delamination, or wear such that store structural integrity is commensurate with the specified service life. (3) Flight test: In tandem with 17.1.2.1 and 17.2.2.1, conduct flight test with a structurally representative instrumented test vehicle that is capable of measuring repeated loads and dynamic environments experienced in flight.
